YouTube: The Dos, Don'ts & Channel-Ending Mistakes

7 min read · Updated November 2026 · Free · Written for Kenya
Share: WhatsApp X Facebook Telegram LinkedIn

That 'I subscribe to you, you subscribe back' deal in your WhatsApp creators' group is named directly in YouTube's spam policy. It isn't a growth hack. It's a strike waiting to happen.

YouTube is the most predictable platform about punishment, because it publishes its ladder. Learn it once and you'll never be surprised.

StageWhat happens
First violationUsually just a warning. Complete YouTube's policy training and the warning expires after 90 days
1st strike1 week with no uploads, live streams, custom thumbnails or Premieres. Lasts 90 days
2nd strike (within 90 days)2 weeks with no posting
3rd strike (within 90 days)The channel can be permanently removed
Severe abuseTermination after a single case, with no warning
DODON'T
Ask viewers to like, subscribe and comment. That's allowedJoin sub4sub groups or view-swap chains
Make titles and thumbnails match what's in the videoPromise 'FULL MATCH' and show a 2-minute clip
Add real commentary, analysis or your own footage when you use clipsRe-upload others' videos 'without adding anything of your own'
Build series where each episode has its own focusMass-produce near-identical template or AI videos
Tick the altered or synthetic content box for realistic AIPass off a realistic AI clip as real footage
Comment as yourself on videos you actually watchedPaste 'check out my channel' across hundreds of videos
Link to your WhatsApp or shop as part of a useful videoMake videos whose only purpose is to send people off YouTube
Set 'made for kids' honestlyMislabel children's content to keep comments and personalised ads
Use the YouTube Audio Library or music you have rights toPut a hit Bongo or gengetone track under your vlog without permission
Vet anyone you hire to promote your channelHire a promoter who sells views. YouTube holds you responsible

What gets channels restricted or terminated

  • Engagement manipulation. Bots, coercion or rewards in exchange for views, likes or subscribers, including coordinated sub-for-sub schemes.
  • Misleading metadata. Titles, thumbnails or descriptions designed to trick people into clicking.
  • Scams. Get-rich-quick schemes, fake job offers and fake 'customer support' numbers.
  • Inauthentic content. Since 15 July 2025, repetitive or mass-produced content (formerly called 'repetitious content') can't be monetised.

The honest risk ladder for bought views

YouTube's fake engagement policy bans promoting services that boost views, likes or subscribers, and its Partner Program policies ban artificially inflating any metric. Here's how it usually escalates:

  1. Count removal. Artificial views don't count and can be stripped from your totals.
  2. Money held. For monetised channels, YouTube can withhold or claw back earnings, with payment delays of up to 90 days while it investigates.
  3. Feature blocks. Strikes freeze uploads for 1 to 2 weeks.
  4. Termination. Removal from the Partner Program, or the channel itself.
✗ MYTH

A copyright claim is the same as a strike.

✓ REALITY

They're different systems. A Content ID claim usually just sends the ad money to the music owner or blocks the video in some countries. A copyright strike comes from a formal takedown request. A Community Guidelines strike comes from breaking rules like spam or harassment. Three of either kind of strike puts a channel at risk.

Kenyan specifics

  • KFCB and online video. In May 2025 the High Court (Justice Mugambi) dismissed Eldoret creator William Getumbe's petition and held that the Films and Stage Plays Act covers any audio-visual recording shown to the public, amateur YouTube videos included. It also said pre-approving every upload is impractical.
  • Filming licences. KFCB's 2026 notices said all filming in Kenya needs prior licensing, and its grace period for productions made from 2018 to 2026 closed on 4 June 2026. How this applies to small creators is still unclear, so commercial and sponsored shoots are the most exposed. Check with KFCB before a big production.
  • Betting sponsors. BCLB's May 2025 rules ban creators from promoting gambling, so turn down that 'sponsored by' read.
✅ Your 10-minute rules audit
⚡ Quick check

Which of these does YouTube's spam policy actually ALLOW?

Asking your own viewers to like, subscribe or comment is fine. Swapping subscriptions, mass comment spam and promoting view sellers are all named as violations, even when the people involved are real.

🧠 Key takeaways
  1. Learn the ladder: a warning, then 1-week and 2-week strikes, then possible termination at 3 strikes in 90 days.
  2. Sub4sub, misleading thumbnails and comment spam are named spam violations.
  3. Fake views don't count, can freeze your earnings, and can end a channel.
  4. In Kenya, a 2025 High Court ruling says film-classification law covers online video.
